[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) in Oracle Database"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) in Oracle Database provides encryption at rest, meaning that data is encrypted when stored on disk. This helps protect sensitive data from unauthorized access in case of physical theft of storage media or unauthorized access to data files. TDE encrypts data in database tables and tablespaces. The encryption is transparent to applications, meaning that applications do not need to be modified to use TDE."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Key Concepts"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"**Data Encryption Key (DEK):** This key encrypts the actual data. It is stored in the data dictionary, encrypted by the TDE master encryption key."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"**TDE Master Encryption Key:** This key encrypts the DEK. It is stored in an external keystore (Oracle Key Vault or Hardware Security Module - HSM) or the Oracle Wallet."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"**Keystore:** A secure storage location for the TDE master encryption key. Oracle recommends using Oracle Key Vault or an HSM for enhanced security. Oracle Wallet is also supported."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Steps to Implement TDE"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"The following steps outline the process of implementing TDE in Oracle Database. This example uses Oracle Wallet as the keystore. For production environments, consider using Oracle Key Vault or an HSM."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Configure the Oracle Wallet"},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"# Create a directory for the wallet
mkdir -p /opt/oracle/admin/tde_wallet

# Set the ENCRYPTION_WALLET_LOCATION parameter in sqlnet.ora
# Add the following line to sqlnet.ora (usually located in $ORACLE_HOME/network/admin)
ENCRYPTION_WALLET_LOCATION=
  (SOURCE=
    (METHOD=FILE)
    (METHOD_DATA=
      (DIRECTORY=/opt/oracle/admin/tde_wallet)))

# Restart the listener
lsnrctl stop
lsnrctl start"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Create the Oracle Wallet"},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"# As the Oracle user, create the wallet using orapki
orapki wallet create -wallet /opt/oracle/admin/tde_wallet -auto_login_only"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Set the TDE Master Encryption Key"},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"# Connect to the database as SYSDBA
sqlplus / as sysdba

# Set the encryption key
ADMINISTER KEY MANAGEMENT CREATE KEYSTORE '/opt/oracle/admin/tde_wallet' IDENTIFIED BY "<wallet_password>";

# Open the keystore
ADMINISTER KEY MANAGEMENT SET KEYSTORE OPEN IDENTIFIED BY "<wallet_password>";

# Create the TDE master encryption key
ADMINISTER KEY MANAGEMENT SET KEY IDENTIFIED BY "<new_master_key_password>" WITH BACKUP;

# Verify the keystore status
SELECT WRL_TYPE, WRL_PARAMETER, STATUS FROM V$ENCRYPTION_WALLET;"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Encrypt a Tablespace"},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"# Create a new tablespace (or use an existing one)
CREATE TABLESPACE encrypted_tablespace DATAFILE '/u02/oradata/ORCL/encrypted_tablespace01.dbf' SIZE 100M ENCRYPTION USING 'AES128' DEFAULT STORAGE (ENCRYPT);

# Verify the tablespace encryption
SELECT TABLESPACE_NAME, ENCRYPTED FROM DBA_TABLESPACES WHERE TABLESPACE_NAME = 'ENCRYPTED_TABLESPACE';"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"5. Encrypt a Column"},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"# Create a table with an encrypted column
CREATE TABLE employees (
  id NUMBER PRIMARY KEY,
  name VARCHAR2(100),
  salary NUMBER ENCRYPT USING 'AES192'
);

# Insert data into the table
INSERT INTO employees (id, name, salary) VALUES (1, 'John Doe', 60000);

# Verify the column encryption
SELECT COLUMN_NAME, ENCRYPTED FROM DBA_TAB_COLUMNS WHERE TABLE_NAME = 'EMPLOYEES' AND COLUMN_NAME = 'SALARY';"},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"6. Re-keying the TDE Master Key"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"It is recommended to periodically re-key the TDE master encryption key for security purposes."},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"# Re-key the TDE master encryption key
ADMINISTER KEY MANAGEMENT SET KEY IDENTIFIED BY "<new_master_key_password>" WITH BACKUP;
"},{"order":22,"type":"subheading","text":"Important Considerations"},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Choose a strong password for the TDE master encryption key."},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Regularly back up the Oracle Wallet or keystore."},{"order":25,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Consider using Oracle Key Vault or an HSM for enhanced security in production environments."},{"order":26,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Monitor the keystore status and audit TDE operations."},{"order":27,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Understand the performance impact of encryption and choose an appropriate encryption algorithm (AES128, AES192, AES256)."}]
